newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: De Beers says staff still in Zaire hotspots.
newsitem.headline: De Beers says staff still in Zaire hotspots.

text.p: Diamond giant De Beers said on Tuesday it still had staff in two Zairean towns which are threatened by rebels fighting to oust the country's President Mobutu Sese Seko.
Rebel forces are closing in on the diamond centres of Mbuji-Mayi and Kisangani, where De Beers has trading offices.
"We have not evacuated our offices in Mbuji-Mayi," said Gary Ralfe, managing director of De Beers's Central Selling Organisation.
Ralfe, speaking at a news conference for De Beer's year results, said the firm also had staff in Kisangani -- a centre of the government army and its foreign mercenaries.
Rebel leader Laurent Kabila has proclaimed Kisangani as his next target, giving Zaire's generals a March 13 deadline to lay down arms.
The governor of the region says rebels have already reached within 100 km (60 miles) of the city in at least two locations to the north.
Ralfe said De Beers would remove its staff from both Kisangani and Mbuji-Mayi if danger threatened. "We are watching the situation carefully and we will evacuate our staff when we have to."
Ralfe added that De Beers had no contacts with the rebels. "We are not in contact with Mr Kabila or his forces."
